1.

Heard Sri Arun Kumar Gupta, learned counsel for the petitioner as well as Sri Vishwanath Nishad,
learned AGA for the State and Sri Sushil Kumar Gupta, learned counsel for opposite parties no.2 to 7.
2.

By means of this petition filed under Section 482 Cr.P.C., the petitioner has prayed the following main reliefs:-
"For fact, reasons and circumstances states in the accompanying affidavit it is most respectfully prayed that this Hon'ble court may kindly be pleased to quash the Charge Smt. Anjali vs State Of U.P. 504 I.P.C & 3/4 D P Act relating to P.S Mahila Thana District Hardoi and also be pleased to quash the entire proceeding of case no. 18995/22 Pending in the court of Civil Judge (JD) FTC (W) Hardoi arising out on the basis of the aforesaid charge sheet in the interest of law and justice.
It is further most respectfully prayed that this Hon'ble court may kindly be pleased to stay the further proceeding of case no. 18995 /22 arising out of case crime no.
39/2022 U/S- 498A, 323, 504, I.P.C & 3/4 DP Act relating to P.S Mahila Thana District Hardoi Pending in the court of Civil Judge (JD) FTC (W) Hardoi during the pending of the present petition in the interest of law and justice."
3.

sentences.text: This Court vide order dated 16.02.2024 directed the parties to appear before the trial court concerned and the trial court was directed to verify the contents and parties of the compromise deed.

4. In compliance of the aforesaid order, compromise deed was filed before the learned Court below i.e. In-charge Civil Judge (J.D.), F.T.C. (Crime Against Women), Hardoi, who vide order/ report dated 06.03.2024 has verified the contents and parties of the compromise deed and submitted report to the extent that the parties and contents of the compromise deed are genuine and they have entered into the compromise by free-will.
5.

entities.text: Civil Judge (J.D.), F.T.C. (Crime Against Women), Hardoi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for opposite party no.2 to 7 has submitted that the parties in dispute are not interested to pursue the criminal case.

6. The Apex Court in re: Unnikrishnan alias Unnikuttan vs. State of Kerala, reported in (2018) 15 Supreme Court Cases 343, has observed that even if the offence(s) in question is / are not compoundable within the scope of Section 320 Cr.P.C. even then considering the facts and circumstances of the case in question the Constitutional Court may allow the parties to compound such offence(s) on the basis of compromise arrived at between the parties.
7.

entities.text: Unnikrishnan alias Unnikuttan vs. State of Kerala, reported in (2018) 15 Supreme Court Cases 343

sentences.text:
Not only the above, considering the facts and circumstances of the issue in question and other dictums of the Apex Court in re: B.S. Joshi and others Vs. State of Haryana and Another; 2003 (4)
SCC 675, Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab (2012) 10 SCC 303; State of Rajasthan vs. Shambhu Kewat,
(2014) 4 SCC 149; State of Madhya Pradesh vs. Deepak (2014) 10 SCC 285; State of Madhya Pradesh vs. Manish (2015) 8 SCC 307; J.Ramesh Kamath vs. Mohana Kurup (2016) 12 SCC 179; State of Madhya Pradesh vs. Rajveer Singh (2016) 12 SCC 471 and Parbatbhai Ahir vs. State of Gujarat (2017) 9 SCC 641, the entire proceedings of the aforesaid criminal case are hereby quashed on the basis of compromise.
